rules: A chat may not write a canonical ref directly.
A chat may write only an isolated candidate branch within an active work lease.
Canonical admission requires both a valid owner-lane lease and the current global repository-writer fence.
Canonical admission must bind expected_base_sha to the live canonical head observed after lease validation.
Canonical ref movement is fast-forward-only compare-and-set; ordinary force mutation is forbidden.
A stale fence epoch is permanently invalid even after lease expiration or worker restart.
A changed owner control head invalidates mutation authority until the operation is revalidated.
Central objective replacement, topology/ownership change, cross-owner canonical write, failed-gate bypass, force mutation and permanent security-policy change require USER_REQUIRED authorization.
A worker cannot widen its own lease or alter its authorization class.
Workflow files targeting self-hosted runners are security-sensitive USER_REQUIRED changes and must never execute from pull_request events.
Untrusted pull-request code must never run on A-01 or another persistent self-hosted runner.
Repository state is the source of truth; chat memory is never sufficient authority for a mutation.
